rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust the agentic design — no human backstops.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L47 "keep the draft a draft" and L25 "Push back when it comes back polished": both are the student judging output, not a human backstop on an agent flow; prompts name agent authority ("Where you're guessing at how our team works, mark it as a question for me").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: One exercise = one bounded activity.
rules_evaluated.evidence: One exercise, one bounded activity: L11 "## Phase 1: Build your piece" then L49 "## Phase 2: Lay the three side by side"; the three role tracks (L17/L27/L37) are unnumbered headings, each student runs one, so no sub-numbering and no stacked activities.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Three-level completeness.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Artifact chain is closed: consumes team/chosen-bet.md (L9), produces prototype / kill-test + fake door / way-of-working (prompts), each sendable ("ready to run on Monday" L31); maintainer Produces line names the downstream readers.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Progression-with-variations is the spine.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Push-back move recurs under a different face per track: L25 polish, L35 accidental threshold, L47 colleague who folds; closest to verbatim repeat is the "Push back" opener, but each names a different object and tell.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Student agency — adults decide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L29 "Write down what would kill the bet before you build anything": an order imposed, but it guards a dead end (a favourite result chosen first) and the fenced prompt carries it; no stopwatch or compulsion prose elsewhere.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Delegation — student brings, Claude screens.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Student picks, Claude proposes: PO prompt "Ask me to pick one"; designer prompt "Ask me two things, one at a time". Closest: L43-prompt "you remember the last change negotiations" gives Claude no access to the team history, but it is role fiction the student corrects, and the draft prompt marks guesses as questions.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Split mega-exercise when phases = distinct skills + distinct artifacts.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Three distinct artifacts but run in parallel by role, one per student, joined at Phase 2 (L49); no mega-exercise per student, so no split owed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Artifact-realism check.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Named files resolve: team/chosen-bet.md and its riskiest assumption come from apt101-d2-write-the-chosen-bet (grep -n "riskiest assumption" -> L20); team/what-goes-in.md is Day 1; <my-name> convention present across apt101-d2 prompts (grep -c shows 2-3 per prompt). Output paths are created by the prompts themselves.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Teach principle + technique — default.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Why and how both present: L25 "A finished look makes people believe the design is further along than it is" (why rough); L35 test card named with its four fields in the prompt. Closest: Jobs to be Done used unnamed (L19), a map not a black box.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Forcing functions stay, scripted reactions go. Forcing functions live in prompts, not body prose.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Mandatory moves are fenced (question-first in designer prompt, test card before build in PO prompt, proposal framing and five-question rehearsal in lead prompts). Closest L25/L35/L47 "Push back ..." are optional refinements the carve-out lets live in body; no bare counts in body (the "five questions" sits in the fence).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Personal-first, team promotion via human conversation.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L47 "the point of Monday is that the team decides with you" and prompt "Write it as a proposal the team decides, not a decision": promotion goes through a human conversation, no auto-promote.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Cohort execution is trainer-paced + concurrent, not sequential.
rules_evaluated.evidence: sed -n 1,58p | grep -E '\*[0-9]+ min\*' -> 35 + 10 = 45 = L3 'Time: 45 minutes'; phase 1 tracks run concurrently, so the budget is the slower track, not a sum.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Host-skill optional; maintainer blocks trainer-only.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -ciE 'Nerd|Teacher Claude|host-skill' over lines 1-58 -> 0; maintainer block names no host-skill actor.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reflection beats: in-chat over file-write.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Files written have named downstream readers (maintainer Produces: imagine it failed, Monday list, Day 3 slice, five users, take it to the team); no reflection-only file. Closest: kill-test.md, read by the Day 3 slice.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Classroom = default delivery; body teaches work, trainer manages room.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L57 "Then one round, piece by piece. The other two point at the part of it that only its maker could have made, and say why. The maker says nothing until both have spoken." It is the beat's designed work (the trio round, maintainer Room: hidden-spine thread 3), defines a mode not a pace, and sibling APT101 group beats carry the same register; no pause-cue, no discuss-with sentence. Rule question: the maker-silent clause is form the trainer could own.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Reading burden for verification = banned. Claude audits Claude.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L25 "Ask Claude to find each quote in the interview files; any it can't find goes.": the verification is now delegated to Claude against the interview files, and the prompt already forces quote plus source onto every screen; the student only decides what stays. Reading burden absent; the earlier suggestion has landed.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-report + self-audit charity — verify at artifact, over-flag or fresh-session for critique.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest prompt "At the end of the page, list what the prototype does not answer" (self-report) and L25 "Ask Claude to find each quote in the interview files; any it can't find goes": verification is at the artifact (quote plus source on every screen), not on Claude's summary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Offered structures need forced-engagement mechanic.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Offered structures carry forced engagement: test-card fields are followed by L35 "Push back on a threshold you could hit by accident"; experiments arrive as three options ending "Ask me to pick one". Closest: the four-field card could be taken verbatim, hence the threshold push-back.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Task selection drives outcome → name floor AND ceiling.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Prompts carry floor and ceiling: "one HTML file", "Rough is right: grey boxes, real words", "two or three of the cheapest experiments", "a one-page working agreement". No too-big-task watch-for in the maintainer block.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Maintainer-block hedge naming section's own failure mode = cut-signal, not warning.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Failure-modes line "the threshold is unfalsifiable" is recoverable by body callout and is: L35. Premise test: removing the hedge leaves the section defensible.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audience tier determines authoring substrate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Product-trio tier: every prompt is a paste into Claude Code (badge "(Claude Code)"), outputs are html/md files, no install step stealing the teaching moment.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Load-bearing platform feature = no fallback. Gate or redesign.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -ciE 'if your (environment|setup)|instead and treat' over lines 1-58 -> 0; the team board in Phase 2 is gated by the training's prework, no fallback offered.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Plug points + UX.
rules_evaluated.evidence: (a) no Plug Points section. (b) UX: walked prompt to prompt as a fast operator, each named file has a producing step (chosen-bet.md from write-the-chosen-bet; what-goes-in.md Day 1; outputs created by the prompts), prompts are single pastes. Closest wait-what: L55 "today's made-up quote" resolves to catch-it-making-things-up (same day), and L53 "bet frame of your team board" resolves to the Day 2 board.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test — 3 observable Monday outcomes.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L76 (maintainer) "Leap test: on Monday each person (1) has a piece only their seat could have made (prototype, kill test, working agreement); (2) can say what it is for in one sentence; (3) can name what the other two pieces need from theirs." Three outcomes, artifact-named per the arc-mood carve-out. Closest to abstract: (2) "can say what it is for", but it is an utterance a working engineer can check on Monday. grep -ci leap -> 1.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-phase failure mode + escape hatch.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L78 Failure modes now covers phase 2 ("nobody says which only one person could have made (each names one)"), designer, threshold, handed-down agreement. Closest gap: "the threshold is unfalsifiable" has no hatch in the block, and the rehearsal's dominant failure (colleague folds after one answer) has no row. Stays PASS: both are student-catchable and their recovery sits in body (L35 "Push back on a threshold you could hit by accident", L47 "Push back on a colleague who folds after one answer"), so the harm (trainer with no move) is absent. Suggestion offers the rows.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Save belongs with authoring, not loading.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Create prompts save to the production location at close: team/<my-name>/prototype.html, kill-test.md, way-of-working.md; no create-then-use pair split across exercises in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Convenience-driven prompts with known shape-bias → body acknowledgment callout.
rules_evaluated.evidence: PO prompt packs propose, pick, card and build in one paste and lets Claude set its own threshold (self-charity risk); the adjacent body callout L35 "Push back on a threshold you could hit by accident" names the tradeoff and steers, so accepted-with-mitigation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body prose must not supply an answer its prompt asks for — position is not the test (widened 2026-08-12).
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L19 "what the thing does in the customer's day, what using it feels like, or whether it can work at all": a menu of question kinds, while the prompt asks the student to pick; it names categories, not the answer. L25 and L35 teach reading a bad answer, the legal shape. L7 lead-in names artifacts and activities only.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Callouts next to prompts: steer, don't pre-empt.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest L25 "Push back when it comes back polished": the prompt already says "Rough is right", but the callout is steering shaped (recognise, push back) and teaches the why, so it does not rot if the prompt changes.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Group beat ≠ parallel solo work.
